lines.text: You tell Kubernetes to keep three copies of a web app running.
lines.caption: You tell Kubernetes to keep three copies of a web app running.

lines.text: At three in the morning, a machine dies, and takes one copy with it.
lines.caption: At three in the morning, a machine dies, and takes one copy with it.

lines.text: Nobody is awake, and nobody runs a command.
lines.caption: Nobody is awake, and nobody runs a command.

lines.text: A few minutes later, there are three copies again.
lines.caption: A few minutes later, there are three copies again.

lines.text: Now take Terraform.
lines.caption: Now take Terraform.

lines.text: You tell it you want five servers, and it creates them.
lines.caption: You tell it you want five servers, and it creates them.

lines.text: Then someone deletes one by hand.
lines.caption: Then someone deletes one by hand.

lines.text: This time nothing happens.
lines.caption: This time nothing happens.

lines.text: Terraform only notices the next time someone runs it.
lines.caption: Terraform only notices the next time someone runs it.

lines.text: Both tools take a description of what you want, and make it real.
lines.caption: Both tools take a description of what you want, and make it real.

lines.text: How do they do that, and keep it that way?
lines.caption: How do they do that, and keep it that way?

lines.text: And why does one repair things by itself, while the other waits for you?
lines.caption: And why does one repair things by itself, while the other waits for you?

lines.text: There are two ways to tell a machine what to do.
lines.caption: There are two ways to tell a machine what to do.

lines.text: You can list the steps: start two more servers.
lines.caption: You can list the steps: start two more servers.

lines.text: Or you can describe the end state: there should be three servers.
lines.caption: Or you can describe the end state: there should be three servers.

lines.text: The difference shows up when you run it twice.
lines.caption: The difference shows up when you run it twice.

lines.text: Here's a script that says "start two more servers".
lines.caption: Here's a script that says "start two more servers".

lines.text: Run it once: two servers.
lines.caption: Run it once: two servers.

lines.text: Run it again: four.
lines.caption: Run it again: four.

lines.text: Every run repeats its work.
lines.caption: Every run repeats its work.

lines.text: Here's Terraform, told there should be three servers.
lines.caption: Here's Terraform, told there should be three servers.

lines.text: The first run creates three.
lines.caption: The first run creates three.

lines.text: Run it again, with nothing changed, and it says: no changes; your infrastructure matches the configuration.
lines.caption: Run it again, with nothing changed, and it says: no changes; your infrastructure matches the configuration.

lines.text: Change the three to five, and it doesn't start five more.
lines.caption: Change the three to five, and it doesn't start five more.

lines.text: It compares what you want with what exists, and plans exactly two.
lines.caption: It compares what you want with what exists, and plans exactly two.

lines.text: Listing the steps is called imperative.
lines.caption: Listing the steps is called imperative.

lines.text: Describing the end state is called declarative.
lines.caption: Describing the end state is called declarative.

lines.text: The end state you describe is the desired state; what exists right now is the current state.
lines.caption: The end state you describe is the desired state; what exists right now is the current state.

lines.text: The tool's job is to make the current state match the desired one.
lines.caption: The tool's job is to make the current state match the desired one.

lines.text: So it's tempting to picture apply like running a script: once it has run, the job is done.
lines.caption: So it's tempting to picture apply like running a script: once it has run, the job is done.

lines.text: But running it again did nothing at all.
lines.caption: But running it again did nothing at all.

lines.text: That wasn't "already ran".
lines.caption: That wasn't "already ran".

lines.text: It was "already matches".
lines.caption: It was "already matches".

lines.text: A thermostat is the classic picture of how that job gets done.
lines.caption: A thermostat is the classic picture of how that job gets done.

lines.text: You set the temperature you want.
lines.caption: You set the temperature you want.

lines.text: The thermostat measures the room, compares, and turns the heating on or off.
lines.caption: The thermostat measures the room, compares, and turns the heating on or off.

lines.text: Then it measures again, and keeps going.
lines.caption: Then it measures again, and keeps going.

lines.text: Kubernetes works the same way.
lines.caption: Kubernetes works the same way.

lines.text: For each kind of thing it manages, a program called a controller runs a loop: look at the desired state, look at the current state, and act on the difference.
lines.caption: For each kind of thing it manages, a program called a controller runs a loop: look at the desired state, look at the current state, and act on the difference.

lines.text: Then do it again.
lines.caption: Then do it again.

lines.text: For the web app, the desired state is three copies.
lines.caption: For the web app, the desired state is three copies.

lines.text: Kubernetes calls that number the replica count, and each running copy a pod.
lines.caption: Kubernetes calls that number the replica count, and each running copy a pod.

lines.text: The controller counts the pods.
lines.caption: The controller counts the pods.

lines.text: If it finds two, it starts one.
lines.caption: If it finds two, it starts one.

lines.text: If it finds four, it deletes one.
lines.caption: If it finds four, it deletes one.

lines.text: If it finds three, it does nothing.
lines.caption: If it finds three, it does nothing.

lines.text: That's what happened at three in the morning.
lines.caption: That's what happened at three in the morning.

lines.text: The dead machine stopped reporting, and within a minute a separate loop, the one that watches machines, marked it as unreachable.
lines.caption: The dead machine stopped reporting, and within a minute a separate loop, the one that watches machines, marked it as unreachable.

lines.text: Its copy then got a grace period, five minutes by default, in case the machine came back.
lines.caption: Its copy then got a grace period, five minutes by default, in case the machine came back.

lines.text: When that ran out, about six minutes after the crash, the copy no longer counted.
lines.caption: When that ran out, about six minutes after the crash, the copy no longer counted.

lines.text: The controller counting pods came up one short, and started a replacement.
lines.caption: The controller counting pods came up one short, and started a replacement.

lines.text: Nobody had to do anything.
lines.caption: Nobody had to do anything.

lines.text: A loop like this is called a reconciliation loop.
lines.caption: A loop like this is called a reconciliation loop.

lines.text: Why count the pods every time?
lines.caption: Why count the pods every time?

lines.text: It would seem cheaper to react to events: when a pod dies, the system sends a "pod died" event, so start one pod.
lines.caption: It would seem cheaper to react to events: when a pod dies, the system sends a "pod died" event, so start one pod.

lines.text: But events get lost.
lines.caption: But events get lost.

lines.text: Here are two controllers keeping three pods running, on the same timeline.
lines.caption: Here are two controllers keeping three pods running, on the same timeline.

lines.text: At second ten, a pod crashes.
lines.caption: At second ten, a pod crashes.

lines.text: Both controllers see it, and both start a replacement.
lines.caption: Both controllers see it, and both start a replacement.

lines.text: At second twenty, each controller is restarted, say for an upgrade, and is down for a few seconds.
lines.caption: At second twenty, each controller is restarted, say for an upgrade, and is down for a few seconds.

lines.text: While it's down, another pod crashes.
lines.caption: While it's down, another pod crashes.

lines.text: The first controller only reacts to events.
lines.caption: The first controller only reacts to events.

lines.text: The "pod died" event arrived while it was down, so it never saw it.
lines.caption: The "pod died" event arrived while it was down, so it never saw it.

lines.text: It never starts a replacement, and stays at two pods for good.
lines.caption: It never starts a replacement, and stays at two pods for good.

lines.text: The second controller doesn't care about events.
lines.caption: The second controller doesn't care about events.

lines.text: When it comes back, it counts two pods, wants three, and starts one.
lines.caption: When it comes back, it counts two pods, wants three, and starts one.

lines.text: The first controller acts on each change; that's called edge-triggered.
lines.caption: The first controller acts on each change; that's called edge-triggered.

lines.text: The second acts on the current state; that's called level-triggered.
lines.caption: The second acts on the current state; that's called level-triggered.

lines.text: Kubernetes' design principles require the second: a controller has to get it right from the desired and current state alone, no matter how many updates it missed.
lines.caption: Kubernetes' design principles require the second: a controller has to get it right from the desired and current state alone, no matter how many updates it missed.

lines.text: Events are only a hint to look again soon.
lines.caption: Events are only a hint to look again soon.

lines.text: That explains how a loop stays right when it misses something.
lines.caption: That explains how a loop stays right when it misses something.

lines.text: It doesn't say how often the loop runs, and that's where the two tools part ways.
lines.caption: It doesn't say how often the loop runs, and that's where the two tools part ways.

lines.text: Both tools reconcile.
lines.caption: Both tools reconcile.

lines.text: The difference is when.
lines.caption: The difference is when.

lines.text: Terraform's command-line tool compares the desired and current state when you run it, and then stops.
lines.caption: Terraform's command-line tool compares the desired and current state when you run it, and then stops.

lines.text: Here it is managing the five servers from before.
lines.caption: Here it is managing the five servers from before.

lines.text: Someone deletes one of them by hand.
lines.caption: Someone deletes one of them by hand.

lines.text: Terraform isn't running, so nothing happens, and it stays deleted.
lines.caption: Terraform isn't running, so nothing happens, and it stays deleted.

lines.text: Terraform keeps its own record of what it created.
lines.caption: Terraform keeps its own record of what it created.

lines.text: The next time someone runs terraform plan, it refreshes that record against what actually exists, finds four, and plans one to add.
lines.caption: The next time someone runs terraform plan, it refreshes that record against what actually exists, finds four, and plans one to add.

lines.text: That's what the script picture gets wrong.
lines.caption: That's what the script picture gets wrong.

lines.text: Applying didn't hold the system there.
lines.caption: Applying didn't hold the system there.

lines.text: Terraform only checks it when you ask.
lines.caption: Terraform only checks it when you ask.

lines.text: A Kubernetes controller's loop has no end.
lines.caption: A Kubernetes controller's loop has no end.

lines.text: It runs all the time, comparing again and again, so a change nobody asked for is repaired on its own: within seconds for a deleted copy, and a few minutes for a dead machine, because of that grace period.
lines.caption: It runs all the time, comparing again and again, so a change nobody asked for is repaired on its own: within seconds for a deleted copy, and a few minutes for a dead machine, because of that grace period.

lines.text: The current state moving away from the desired state is called drift.
lines.caption: The current state moving away from the desired state is called drift.

lines.text: With Terraform, drift waits for the next run.
lines.caption: With Terraform, drift waits for the next run.

lines.text: With a continuous loop, drift is repaired as soon as the loop notices.
lines.caption: With a continuous loop, drift is repaired as soon as the loop notices.

lines.text: Change the web app from three copies to five, and apply it with cube control, Kubernetes' command-line tool.
lines.caption: Change the web app from three copies to five, and apply it with kubectl, Kubernetes' command-line tool.

lines.text: It answers at once: configured.
lines.caption: It answers at once: configured.

lines.text: But only three of the five copies are ready.
lines.caption: But only three of the five copies are ready.

lines.text: A moment later, four.
lines.caption: A moment later, four.

lines.text: Then five.
lines.caption: Then five.

lines.text: That count comes from a field called status, where Kubernetes reports the current state it has observed.
lines.caption: That count comes from a field called status, where Kubernetes reports the current state it has observed.

lines.text: Applying records what you want.
lines.caption: Applying records what you want.

lines.text: Getting there is separate, and slower.
lines.caption: Getting there is separate, and slower.

lines.text: Sometimes it never happens, if a copy can't start at all.
lines.caption: Sometimes it never happens, if a copy can't start at all.

lines.text: To know a change took effect, you look at the status, not at the apply.
lines.caption: To know a change took effect, you look at the status, not at the apply.

lines.text: The loop doesn't promise to settle, either.
lines.caption: The loop doesn't promise to settle, either.

lines.text: If the desired state keeps changing, it chases a moving target.
lines.caption: If the desired state keeps changing, it chases a moving target.

lines.text: And two tools can want different values for the same field.
lines.caption: And two tools can want different values for the same field.

lines.text: An autoscaler changes the number of copies to match the load.
lines.caption: An autoscaler changes the number of copies to match the load.

lines.text: Meanwhile, a job that re-applies your file every few minutes sets it back to the number written there.
lines.caption: Meanwhile, a job that re-applies your file every few minutes sets it back to the number written there.

lines.text: They can undo each other's work over and over.
lines.caption: They can undo each other's work over and over.

lines.text: And nothing repairs what no tool manages.
lines.caption: And nothing repairs what no tool manages.

lines.text: A setting changed by hand on something outside the configuration is simply invisible to it.
lines.caption: A setting changed by hand on something outside the configuration is simply invisible to it.

lines.text: So how do these tools turn a description into reality and keep it there?
lines.caption: So how do these tools turn a description into reality and keep it there?

lines.text: You declare the state you want.
lines.caption: You declare the state you want.

lines.text: A loop keeps comparing it with what exists, and fixes the difference, like a thermostat.
lines.caption: A loop keeps comparing it with what exists, and fixes the difference, like a thermostat.

lines.text: It compares whole states instead of reacting to events: level-triggered, not edge-triggered.
lines.caption: It compares whole states instead of reacting to events: level-triggered, not edge-triggered.

lines.text: So a missed event is caught on the next pass.
lines.caption: So a missed event is caught on the next pass.

lines.text: And it aims at an absolute target, so running it again does no harm.
lines.caption: And it aims at an absolute target, so running it again does no harm.

lines.text: Kubernetes repairs things by itself because its loops never stop.
lines.caption: Kubernetes repairs things by itself because its loops never stop.

lines.text: Terraform's command-line tool waits for you because it compares only when you run it.
lines.caption: Terraform's command-line tool waits for you because it compares only when you run it.

lines.text: Either way, what you get is eventual agreement, not an instant guarantee: check the status, and watch for things no tool is managing.
lines.caption: Either way, what you get is eventual agreement, not an instant guarantee: check the status, and watch for things no tool is managing.
